label: nyiso 87 arm C-MEAS measured min-run
definition: nyiso-87 (KEEPER): the nyiso-81 keeper recipe re-solved on current main with two deltas, neither fitted to a residual. (1) the h14-21 peak-window reliability-floor limbs are OFF by owner directive 2026-07-27 (the five enabled evening ramp families, via iso_configs.NYISO_PEAK_WINDOW_FLOORS_OFF; the two unwindowed in-city persistent bases and the Capital_Hudson hot step are kept, outside the directive's scope). (2) nyiso_gas_commitment_bridge armed as the REPLACEMENT (rule 19, substitution not stacking): the third P1-native commitment bridge, with a new minimum-run-duration leg set to the MEASURED CAMPD capacity-weighted p50 per class (min_load_frac CC_REGULAR 0.523 / ST_GAS 0.239, min_run CC_REGULAR 21 h / ST_GAS 13 h, all from one frozen derive). HEADLINE: this closes NYISO's load-bearing C1 FAIL — 2023 CC_REGULAR walks -4.11 -> -2.78 TWh against a +/-2.94 TWh band, with td_loss_factor still 0.0 — while forcing LESS overall than the run it replaces (2023 CT_PEAKER+ST_GAS+CC_REGULAR forced 4.46 -> 4.18 TWh) and improving every class's diurnal shape (CT_PEAKER, never floored by the bridge, cv_ratio 5.12/4.24/2.37 -> 1.38/1.07/1.15). GATES: C1/C2/C3a/C3b/C4/C6/C7/C8 all PASS (C8 2024 ST_GAS 31.9% forced, above the 30% cap but GROUNDED — D-4 clears, D-1 shape clears). C5a 2025 +7.6% CO2 CAVEAT (within commercial band). C3c FAILs — 3/0/6 h >$300 vs actual 10/12/42 — roof-blocked (nyiso-85 §7d) rather than tightness-blocked, recorded not reverted per rule 1. DETERMINATION: NOT-YET (C3c the sole blocking criterion), the most structurally faithful run producible on current main.
market_story: CC_REGULAR (+1.34 TWh vs the prior keeper, 31.19 -> 32.52 in 2023, closing the C1 cell): a real NYISO combined cycle committed for the evening peak does not shut down through the belly and restart — its minimum run duration and the cost of a restart hold it online at minimum stable load, so it is synchronised and ready when the ramp comes. The continuous-variable LP pays no startup and honours no run window, so it cycled these units off and bought the belly from the seam instead; the bridge restores the commitment, and the energy the class gains is energy it was always economically entitled to and physically committed for. Measured corroboration: NYISO CCs actually run 21 h at the capacity-weighted median (CAMPD 2023-2025), against the 5-10 h the model's class table assumed. ST_GAS (-0.37 TWh, and 36.2 -> 31.9 % forced): NYC and Long Island steam still carries a genuine 24-hour in-city voltage/local-reliability commitment — that base stays — but it does NOT additionally get pushed up every afternoon by a temperature boxcar. The measured fleet turns down to 24 % of its high load and holds ~13 h runs, far shorter than the 24-48 h the class table asserted, so the model was over-committing these boilers and under-committing the CCs that should have been serving the peak. CT_PEAKER (1.42 -> 0.46 TWh, 81/86/48 % forced -> 0 %): a downstate peaker's whole economic identity is that it starts in an hour and runs when prices justify it. The h14-21 must-run asserted it runs every summer afternoon regardless — which is why the model showed ~0 MW off-window against a real smooth 58 -> 659 MW ramp. Removing the assertion makes its SHAPE right (off-peak volatility ratio 5.1 -> 1.4) and reveals that the model has no mechanism giving peakers a reason to run at all: the remaining 1.8 TWh gap is a missing NYISO 10-minute reserve / AS story, openly declared rather than bought back with a floor. IMPORTS (belly 3,048 -> 2,797 MW, peak 2,381 -> 2,713 MW vs actual 2,596 / 2,857): NYISO's monthly import volume is pinned, so the only question is WHICH hours it is bought in. Real NYISO buys into the evening peak; the model bought overnight because its internal price curve was too flat to make peak imports attractive. Holding committed gas at min-load through the belly steepens that curve and the pinned volume relocates peak-ward on its own — through the existing hub-priced seam, with nothing in the bridge touching the interchange node.
